rationale: Crawler landed on a PDP (ends with .html), so PLP tiles never appeared. Normalizing any PDP URL to its parent category path reliably yields the PLP on moncler.com (e.g., .../short-down-jackets/<product>.html -> .../short-down-jackets). Adding consent click and a resilient tile wait selector increases the chance tiles render. Host/locale normalization prevents locale traps and corporate site misroutes.
code_hints:
Add a PDP-to-PLP fallback before PLP extraction:
- If location.pathname.endsWith('.html') OR document.querySelector('meta[property="og:type"][content="product"]') OR JSON-LD contains "@type":"Product", then compute parent = url.replace(/\/[^\/]+\.html(\?.*)?$/, '/'); navigate to parent and retry PLP extraction.
On page load, attempt cookie consent: await page.$('#onetrust-accept-btn-handler').then(el => el?.click()).catch(()=>{});

After navigation to PLP, wait for tiles: await page.waitForSelector('.product-grid a[href$=".html"], [data-testid="product-grid"] a[href$=".html"]', { timeout: 12000 }); Then incremental scroll to trigger lazy-load before reading tiles.
Guard against wrong domain: if new URL host ends with 'monclergroup.com', abort and revert to last good PLP.
Only treat links ending with '.html' under /en-de/ as PDPs when collecting product links from PLP.
